item.research_question: How does the addition of CoCrCuFeTi High Entropy Alloy (HEA) as a reinforcement through Friction Stir Processing (FSP) affect the tribological behavior of Stainless Steel (SS304)?
item.material_system: CoCrCuFeTi High Entropy Alloy (HEA) reinforced SS304
item.processing_route: Friction Stir Processing (FSP) with a tungsten carbide tool rotating at 1000 rpm, traverse speed of 25 mm/min, and a load of 10 kN, followed by annealing at 650 °C for 2 h
item.test_conditions: Pin-on-disc wear test with varying load (10-40N), sliding velocity (0.5–3.5 m/s), and sliding distance (500–2000 m)
key_findings: The processed sample with HEA after annealing offered 29.8%, 57.4%, and 58.49% improved wear resistance at the minimum level of load, sliding velocity, and sliding distance than the processed base samples
The worn surface morphology revealed delamination, abrasion, adhesion, and oxide layer formation as the predominant wear mechanisms

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does the addition of CoCrCuFeTi High Entropy Alloy (HEA) as a reinforcement through Friction Stir Processing (FSP) affect the tribological behavior of Stainless Steel (SS304)?. System: CoCrCuFeTi High Entropy Alloy (HEA) reinforced SS304. Processing: Friction Stir Processing (FSP) with a tungsten carbide tool rotating at 1000 rpm, traverse speed of 25 mm/min, and a load of 10 kN, followed by annealing at 650 °C for 2 h. Test conditions: Pin-on-disc wear test with varying load (10-40N), sliding velocity (0.5–3.5 m/s), and sliding distance (500–2000 m). Findings: The processed sample with HEA after annealing offered 29.8%, 57.4%, and 58.49% improved wear resistance at the minimum level of load, sliding velocity, and sliding distance than the processed base samples; The worn surface morphology revealed delamination, abrasion, adhesion, and oxide layer formation as the predominant wear mechanisms; The addition of HEA particles induced dislocation and hindered grain growth, leading to improved microhardness and wear resistance. Mechanism: The authors propose that the improved wear resistance is due to the synergistic effect of the ultrafine refined grains by the FSP process and the stress relieved microstructures after annealing, as well as the dislocation-strengthening mechanism involved in the process. Quote: "The processed samples exhibited excellent refinement in grains with uniform HEA reinforcement distribution"
